We have applied first template 324324, got two precursors: product1: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc1ccccc1N". That seems plausible: the amide part broken to an aniline? Actually original had ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (anilide with an extra NH). The template likely cleaves the amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline with NH2? The result gave "Nc1ccccc1N" (para-diaminobenzene? Actually it's an aniline with an extra N? It's an aniline with an NH2 at both positions? The SMILES "Nc1ccccc1N" is p-phenylenediamine (two amino groups). Good.

Now second template 1914396 applied to the first precursor (the sulfonyl phenyl with a C=O O). It gave two precursors: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So we broke the double bond and carboxylic acid? Actually we got a phenyl aldehyde and a dicarboxylic acid (malonic acid). Good.

Now third template 733 must be applied to something. Likely to the first product "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" to break the sulfonamide? Or to the second product "O=C(O)CC(=O)O" to get something else? Need to apply template 733 to appropriate intermediate to eventually get simple building blocks.

We need at least 3 reactions, we have 2 so far. The third template must be applied to one of the current precursors to further break down. Probably apply to the sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde to break the sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride? Not sure.

Let's check if template 733 matches the aldehyde-containing sulfonyl phenyl. Use check tool.
